title: Pro-environmental behavior

definition.text: Behaviour people consciously choose to reduce the harm their actions do to the environment.

facts.text: Green consumption, buying in ways that harm the environment as little as possible, is one form of it.
Money incentives, costs, regulations and policy norms, along with how much time, money and power people feel they have, shape it through their attitudes.
Barriers to it can be psychological, social or cultural, financial, or structural, such as a home location that forces car dependency.
A meta-analysis confirmed a strong correlation between nature connectedness and pro-environmental behaviour, but found a weaker causal role than assumed.
Climate change narratives told as stories were better at inspiring it in a 2019 study.
Environmental psychology studies the psychological factors behind it and how to encourage it to mitigate climate change and biodiversity loss.

notes: Phrase concept; the page Barriers to pro-environmental behaviour (crawled, another chapter) supplies the definition.
